reason: S1 introduces a stateful SHA-256 hasher API, but H0 compiles only AUX/JSON and JSON modules and exclusively exercises wuffs_json__decoder and wuffs_aux::DecodeJson. Consequently, none of the hasher's byte-processing, buffering, incremental-update, finalization, or quirk methods are reached. The omitted state protocol is material because behavior depends on update partitioning, buf_len across 64-byte blocks, and checksum padding on either side of the 56-byte boundary.
evidence: H0 defines WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__AUX__BASE, WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__AUX__JSON, WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__BASE, and WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__JSON, but no SHA256 module.
H0's fuzz_complex and fuzz_simple call wuffs_json__decoder__decode_tokens, while fuzz_cpp calls wuffs_aux::DecodeJson; no identifier from S1's hasher appears in H0.
S1 adds public entry points hasher.update!, hasher.update_bitvec256!, hasher.checksum_bitvec256, hasher.get_quirk, and hasher.set_quirk!.

hasher.update! retains partial input in buf_data and buf_len, invokes up! at 64-byte boundaries, and updates length_modulo_u64 and length_overflows_u64, creating stateful call-sequence semantics absent from H0.
hasher.checksum_bitvec256 copies buffered state and has distinct padding paths for buf_len < 56 and buf_len >= 56, including a possible second block.
recommended_action: Add a SHA-256-specific harness that compiles the SHA256 module and drives the public hasher API with arbitrary bytes and call sequences. Compare one-shot versus variably chunked update! calls, exercise zero-length updates and lengths around 56 and 64 bytes, call checksum_bitvec256 repeatedly and between later updates, verify update_bitvec256! agrees with update! followed by checksum_bitvec256, and exercise get_quirk/set_quirk! status behavior.
